answer: To halt Sybil attacks, the protocol treats execution bandwidth as a contested meadow requiring dynamic security deposits. New identities start in an isolated haven with zero voting weight and must burn proof-of-work to generate an indelible identity pigment. Colluding nodes detected during sortition audits suffer 100% deposit slashing. An attacker creating 1,000 fake identities pays 100,000 credits in non-refundable burns, ensuring the marginal cost of identity multiplication strictly exceeds any potential extraction value.
